newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble steady on non-resident T-bill investing.
newsitem.headline: Rouble steady on non-resident T-bill investing.

text.p: The rouble was steady in quiet trading ahead of Russia's May Day holidays, buoyed by demand for rouble funds from non-residents to invest in Treasury bills, dealers said.
Markets are closed on May 1 and 2 for the May Day holidays followed by Victory Day on May 9.
On April 30, the finance ministry will auction 7.5 trillion roubles of 322-day GKO discount Treasury bills and 4.0 trillion roubles of two-year OFZ government bonds.
roubles/dollar Apr 29 midday Apr 29 early Apr 28 close

"The market is sticking to the lower limit of the central bank's (dollar) rates. The central bank is trying to push the dollar up but the upward trend is unlikely until non-residents lose interest in T-bills," TOKObank dealer Pavel Shirshov said.
Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said the rouble had edged down in late trading as banks were seeking dollars for current needs, such as position-squaring.
